G0912.name: Barabbas
G0912.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G0912.brief: A notorious prisoner released instead of Jesus.
G0912.short: Barabbas, a notorious prisoner, was released by Pilate instead of Jesus at the crowd's demand.

G0919.name: Bar-jesus
G0919.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G0919.brief: A Jewish sorcerer who opposed Paul and Barnabas.
G0919.short: Bar-Jesus, also known as Elymas, was a Jewish sorcerer who tried to hinder Paul and Barnabas' ministry.

G0921G.name: Barnabas
G0921G.desc: Levite living at the time of the New Testament
G0921G.brief: A Levite from Cyprus who accompanied Paul on missionary journeys.
G0921G.short: Barnabas, also known as Joseph or Joses, was a Levite from Cyprus who played a significant role in the early church and accompanied Paul on missionary journeys.

G0918.name: Bartholomew
G0918.desc: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
G0918.brief: One of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ.
G0918.short: Bartholomew was one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.

G0924.name: Bartimaeus
G0924.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G0924.brief: A blind beggar healed by Jesus near Jericho.
G0924.short: Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was healed by Jesus as He was leaving Jericho.

G0959.name: Bernice
G0959.desc: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
G0959.brief: Jewish princess, sister of King Agrippa II
G0959.short: Bernice, a Jewish princess and sister of King Agrippa II, heard Paul's defense.

G0986.name: Blastus
G0986.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G0986.brief: Herod's chamberlain who helped the people of Tyre and Sidon
G0986.short: Blastus, Herod's chamberlain, was persuaded by the people of Tyre and Sidon to help them gain the king's favor.

G0960.name: Berea
G0960.brief: City in Macedonia where Paul preached; home of Sopater.
G0960.short: Berea was a city in Macedonia where Paul preached, and the home of Sopater, one of Paul's traveling companions.

G0963G.name: Bethany
G0963G.brief: Village near Jerusalem, home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus.
G0963G.short: Bethany was a village near Jerusalem, known as the home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus, where Jesus often visited and performed miracles. (Multiple references, see article for details)

G0964.name: Bethesda
G0964.brief: Pool in Jerusalem where Jesus healed a paralyzed man.
G0964.short: Bethesda (Bethzatha) was a pool in Jerusalem with five roofed colonnades, where Jesus healed a man who had been an invalid for thirty-eight years. (<ref="Jhn.5.2">Jhn.5.2</ref>)

G0967.name: Bethphage
G0967.brief: Village near Bethany, where Jesus began His triumphal entry.
G0967.short: Bethphage was a village near Bethany, where Jesus sent His disciples to find a donkey and a colt for His triumphal entry into Jerusalem.

G0966.name: Bethsaida
G0966.brief: Town where Jesus performed miracles, home of several disciples
G0966.short: Bethsaida was a fishing village on the Sea of Galilee, notable as the hometown of several of Jesus' disciples and a place where He performed miracles.

G0978.name: Bithynia
G0978.short: Bithynia, a region in Asia Minor, where Paul attempted to go but was prevented by the Holy Spirit.
